chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim from 'Ali from Abu Basir said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who spoke to his wife while he was fasting in the month of Ramadan, and he emitted pre-seminal fluid (al-manī), so he said, 'There is no harm.'
ai.seo_question: Does speaking to or being intimate with one's wife while fasting break the fast if only pre-seminal fluid is emitted?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that mere emission of pre-seminal fluid (al-manī) during permissible intimacy does not invalidate the fast, distinguishing it from seminal fluid (al-dhurā') which breaks it. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the specific nature of the discharge rather than the act itself, providing practical clarity for worshippers during Ramadan. The hadith underscores the principle of ease in fasting obligations when the primary condition of intentional consumption or full emission is not met.
